ai.description: This snake reaches 1 meter. It has a distinct bicolored body, yellow ventrally and black dorsally, with a paddle-shaped tail and a flattened body. It lacks ventral scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Yellow-bellied Sea Snake is uniquely identified by its distinct bicolored pattern: a jet-black dorsal side sharply contrasting with a bright yellow or cream-colored belly.
ai.habitat: The yellow-bellied sea snake inhabits warm, pelagic surface waters of the Indian Ocean, typically remaining far from shore and avoiding coastal vegetation or land.
ai.behavior: The yellow-bellied sea snake is a surface-dweller that hunts by drifting with ocean currents, waiting for small fish to seek shelter near its body before striking.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hydrophis platurus* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to 2–6 live young at sea. Breeding occurs year-round in tropical waters, often peaking during warmer months.
ai.distributionRemarks: The yellow-bellied sea snake is a pelagic species found in the coastal waters surrounding the entire Indian subcontinent, from the Arabian Sea to the Bay of Bengal.
